props.title: Three Sweeps, One Missing Layer
props.subtitle: Sweep findings, the sequencing call, and the five-wire backlog

props.content: We mapped Josh's vocabulary against lev's, then audited both sides against reality. Verdict: the engines are real, the compiler is real — but the layer that wires declared control into those engines was never started. Same disease on both sides of the coin: his runtime is prose, ours is stubs. Below: the evidence, the plan, and the backlog that starts fixing it.

FINDINGS
props.title: The three sweeps
props.subtitle: Each ran as an independent agent; full evidence files in the session scratchpad.

props.title: 📖 Wiki glossary sweep
props.content: Josh's 456-page wiki, his own words with citations. **PARK: zero occurrences** — purgatory, mesh, and SCC absent too; all iMessage-only vocabulary he never committed to doctrine. What IS concrete: the **graveyard** — 46 deliberate kill-tests ("failed branches define the obstruction boundary"). He **explicitly forbids loose 'surprise'** (formal FEP only). New HIGH collision found: **canonical**. And his dictionary supports admissibility-not-truth verbatim.

props.title: 🧬 DNA reality census
props.content: JP's "75% done" holds for the **compiler layer**; the whole declared surface is **25–30% fires**. All 44 gates.yaml gates: prose checklist injected into hooks, no code executes their check fields. ~200 flow files compile but the executor is literally `flow-executor-stub.ts`. The scheduling runtime (loader + cron ticker + init) is complete — and no daemon boots it. C4/C5 constraint enforcer: "declared vaporware" by graph.yaml's own admission.

props.title: 🔁 Core-loop audit
props.content: `lev exec --until` runs today — but it **trusts the agent**: the until-condition is pasted into the prompt and the loop exits when the agent says DONE (a text scan of the last 20 lines). `confidence_threshold` exists in the types and is never read. The iterative runner imports **zero** eval code — VERIFY_GATE is a separate system. The SDLC overlay YAML says about itself: "this mechanism does not exist in the executor yet." Tmux: solid SDK, no `lev tmux` CLI. No daemon anywhere.

props.content: Nothing wires declared control into the engines that exist. That's "I can't get a loop to work," explained structurally: the pieces are done — the wiring layer was never started.

The seven instances, each found independently: **pack policies** are never parsed into the grader · **the loop** never calls the grader · **flows** compile but never execute · **schedules** load but never tick · **gates** declare checks nothing runs · **overlays** are specced but never spliced · **the predictor** is built but never bound to the reconciler.

Same verdict for Josh's side, different material: his math-verification program is disciplined and real (73/73 deterministic harness, 4 engines cross-validated, visible withdrawals) — and his runtime architecture is prose. His repo is requirements + evidence; lev is the runtime. The world model is where they meet, and neither side has one yet.

Sources: `lev-dna-reality-census.md` · `core-loop-gap-audit.md` · `josh-wiki-glossary.md` (session scratchpad) · canon doc `.lev/pm/designs/vernacular-exercise.md` §8.

props.label: VOCABULARY
props.title: Glossary reveals
props.subtitle: From Josh's own wiki, in his own words — the corrections that change how we talk.

props.title: 🅿️ PARK isn't doctrine
props.content: Zero occurrences in his wiki. Purgatory too. Mesh: only inside an external pytorch reference. SCC: absent — our `cr_scc_quotient_parity` pack name came from his code bundle, not his doctrine. The (M, W, L, PARK) world-state tuple is conversation vocabulary, never committed. JP's "park WHAT?" was the right question.

props.title: ⚡ Surprise: ours is the loose one
props.content: His dictionary: FEP is "NOT a metaphor for 'the system tries to minimize surprisal'" — formal quantity only. Lev's reconciler surprise (bootstrap = a hash-changed bit) is exactly the loose usage he forbids. If both stay, **ours** takes the qualifier or rename: *change gate*, *delta trigger*. Still owed: where JP's reactor idea came from (F4).

props.title: 📛 Canonical: new HIGH collision
props.content: Lev says "canonical spec / canon / dna" loosely everywhere. His *canonical-by-process* is the strictest status in his system — earned only when **all five** process criteria pass simultaneously, "never assigned from one criterion alone." Same word, completely different weight. Needs a ruling before shared docs use it.

props.title: ✅ Admissibility: already convergent
props.content: His own dictionary: "Admitted = not yet excluded under C… these are not binary final states." Admission means *survived so far*, never *proven correct* — which is JP's truth→admissibility directive, citable from Josh's side. The wording swap in our docs is now just mechanical.
